title: Reviews implied it was all free
body:
Read the reviews and was really impressed to finally have a free app with rave reviews… the free content is good, not sure it’s tailored exactly to ADHD brains as the examples show people being able to adopt techniques first time and change from then on. But they are useful ideas 
Sadly I can’t afford to subscribe for the further content.

body: To use this app you have to pretend you don’t have ADHD. At least there is a 2x button on the video content but essentially the app is the equivalent of telling a depressed person to cheer up.

title: Disappointed
body:
I thought other reviews said this app was totally free but it is asking for
A yearly or monthly subscription.  That is 
Very misleading.

Low star rating due to publishing misleading info to what can be classed as a likely app vulnerable people will use.
author: #Big Momma

title: Fantastic app
body:
I’ve had this app for less than a day and I am so impressed. I’ve tried so many apps and I find them all really overwhelming with info strategies and check lists etc and I end up giving up.

I love that it’s small simple things that your teaching  and can’t believe how easy these things are that are life changing. I am putting everything into practice and it’s working! 

I did think once your completed all what’s on the app then you get to a paid version to access more but from comments I see that’s not the case so I really look forward to see how this develops and what they bring next.

Thankyou
author: Fab Product

title: Life changing
body: Amazing has really helped me focus and feel at ease. Technique simple but effective. Great app highly recommend.
author: mynameis...sam

title: Great app, that’s free with no ads!
body: I really like this app although it would be cool to have additional features that can be added for a fee like cleaning checklists, maybe a podcast or to do list to save using multiple apps to aim to organise my life!!
author: suzsto

title: Excellent and completely free
body: I downloaded a few similar apps but then after going through loads of questions they want you to pay £50-£100 a year and I can’t afford that. This app though is completely free. It has less content than the paid apps but all the content I’ve seen so far has been useful in helping me manage my ADHD symptoms. I’m excited to see it develop further although I’m a little concerned how the developers will afford to do so without revenue from subscriptions or ads.
